charter:
# Charter — T10 SAFe cadence and MSP tranches (retrospective)

Project 01a1d039-0d36-70c1-a5e8-f50956c5e3f9 is the conveyor's T10 slice, "SAFe cadence and MSP tranches", specified in docs/SPEC_V2.md §12 and elaborated in §8.2 (SAFe as the programme cadence) and §8.3 (MSP as the programme definition and benefits realization). It belongs to tranche 4 (01a1e9e0-f4c0-727d-9afb-bb5b1e9783ce), depends on T1 (the plan spine), T3 (the PM job) and the P0 programme record set, and its register row is closed at version 15, created 2026-11-12T14:46:02Z and updated 2026-11-24T17:04:34Z. Its two linked issues, #82 "T10 — SAFe cadence and MSP tranches" and #502 "benefits: a realized status needs a measured transition", are both closed.

Mandate. T10 exists so that planning is arithmetic rather than opinion and so that a programme's tranche and benefit records refuse to pass on free text: WSJF is computed from the four typed inputs and never stored; an approved PI plan materialises the backlog into cards within WIP; a deliverable cannot demo without typed evidence; a retro cannot close while a finding lacks a lesson; an end-of-tranche review must cite baselines, benefit status and risk evidence; and a benefit transition cannot report realization without a measured baseline. The gate text is the one the project row and acceptance/programme/T10.toml carry.

Scope. The slice owns the SAFe cadence machinery (PI planning, system demo, inspect and adapt, backlog refinement), the WSJF arithmetic, the MSP tranche rows and their reviews, and the benefit transition record. It reuses T1's wbs_node, project_baseline, project_register_item and shared_config rather than duplicating them. It does not own the decision ladder (T2), metrics and metering (T11), the one-organisation-loop acceptance (T12), or the meeting types (T19), whose binding to the board and cadence is a follow-up integration unit per §12.

This retrospective is executed under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14, as the tranche-4 rework requested by #526. It publishes the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts with authored bodies, the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract, the project's one accepted WBS deliverable and a Phase-G compliance review, and records the project's expected outputs, project-brief and evidence. It publishes the closure and the closure review for the 2026-11-24 re-close: T10 delivered the cadence and tranche machinery recorded below, on the evidence of acceptance/programme/T10.toml and the named suites, and the re-close keeps the register status closed.

What this retrospective does NOT attest. It does not attest that the §12 gate was run or passed contemporaneously, and it did not re-run the named test suites (their names are carried from the project's recorded artefact entries). It does not attest a tranche-4 exit review: the tranche row is declared authorised, but tranche reconciliation records authorised:false with the flags review_missing and projects_closed_before_authorisation, and the exit criteria — every tranche-4 project accepted with published evidence, and a recorded continue, pause or stop — are not met. It does not attest that the eight recorded findings v1-p82-5, v1-p82-6 and v1-p83-1 to v1-p83-6 are closed. It does not attest a realized programme benefit: the seven benefit profiles are baselined, but benefit_transitions is empty and no post-transition measurement is recorded. It does not attest an approved tranche-4 PI plan: the PI cadence 01a202a1-dbb9-7e49-b64a-cf97c3fab095 is awaiting approval even though the PI plan and PI objectives documents 01a211c9-1346-7108-9a44-667ebf08b50f and 01a211c9-13ae-73b9-a6cd-e31f3a45ca33 are published. Finally, the WSJF inputs 10/13/10/8 recorded by the tranche-4 refinement cadence 01a202a2-2705-7392-a2d1-03ca2b3a174e are the planning record; the approved scope baseline 01a20289-7be3-7e47-afe0-f6b1f82f1892 froze the deliverable at 8/7/8/8, and this pass records the refinement rather than re-measuring the baseline.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T10 SAFe cadence and MSP tranches (retrospective, U5a)

body.assignment: Rework the V2 slice T10 (docs/SPEC_V2.md §8.2, §8.3 and §12; issues #82 and #502) by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle. Produce and publish the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts with authored bodies, the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract; record the project's one WBS deliverable at the tranche-4 refinement's WSJF inputs; take the Phase-G compliance review against the §12 gate; and publish the project's expected outputs, project-brief and evidence. The project's register status is closed at version 15; this pass records the lifecycle retrospectively and re-closes the project on 2026-11-24 with a new closure and closure review, on the evidence of acceptance/programme/T10.toml and the named suites.
body.scope: In scope: the programme_cadence state machine and its PI, demo, retro and refinement kinds; WSJF computed from four typed inputs and never stored; WIP-bounded materialisation behind an approved PI plan, with pending and rejected plans materialising nothing; the demo credit and its typed evidence; the retro lesson rule; the programme_tranche and programme_tranche_review record; and the benefit_transition baseline gate. Out of scope: the T2 decision ladder, the T1 plan-spine baseline contract, the T4 coach card except the retro card, T11 metrics and metering, T12's one-organisation-loop acceptance, and T19's meeting types.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect (conveyor-e2e) owns the slice and authored this retrospective. conveyor-approver is the approver of the Statement of Architecture Work, the delivery contract and the Phase-G review. The Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board) reviews the seven A–D artefacts. The SRO and BCM are accountable for the tranche exit and for benefit ownership, with benefit ownership still a free-text role rather than a job key. The ART and board operator run the PI and accept the materialised cards and the demo; product owners own the backlog and its refinement; project managers supply the accepted evidence the demo credit reads.
body.acceptance_criteria: The SPEC_V2 §12 T10 gate is assessed clause by clause. The Phase-G verdict this pass records is consistent: the lifecycle set and the contract evidence exist, but clause 4 is unproved and clause 1 is partial, so the record does not support compliant or higher. Clause 1, PI planning materialises cards from the backlog by WSJF within WIP, is proved for a project backlog by crates/store/tests/programme_cadence.rs::wsjf_is_computed_not_stored (line 179) and ::materialisation_respects_wip_slots (line 215), with crates/actions/tests/pi_plan_approval.rs::an_approved_plan_materialises_exactly_once (line 297) and apps/server/tests/cadence_jobs.rs::pi_tick_is_idempotent (line 153); it is not proved for the programme's standing backlog, which v1-p82-5 records as pinned to one project_id. Clause 2, a deliverable without evidence cannot demo, is proved by crates/store/tests/demo_gate.rs::a_credit_needs_typed_evidence (line 94) with crates/actions/tests/demo_credit.rs (lines 154 and 168). Clause 3, retro produces lessons, is proved by crates/store/tests/retro.rs::retro_cannot_close_without_lessons (line 190) and ::every_finding_becomes_a_lesson (line 156), with the evidence-free lesson gap v1-p82-6. Clause 4, an end-of-tranche review without baselines, benefit status or risk evidence is refused, has a named passing test, crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_review_without_evidence_is_refused (line 208), but is unproved at HEAD because v1-p83-1 shows free-text placeholders satisfy the three keys and the seed authorises a tranche with no review, and v1-p83-4 shows baseline_ref is nullable and an unapproved baseline satisfies the existence check. Clause 5, a transition that never measured its baseline cannot report the benefit realized, is proved by crates/store/tests/benefit_transition.rs::a_missing_baseline_cannot_claim_realization (line 194) and ::a_measured_baseline_enables_realization (line 161), with the untyped value gap v1-p83-2 and the free-text ownership gap v1-p83-3. The findings are carried open; the acceptance instrument is acceptance/programme/T10.toml.
body.contract: The delivery contract 'Delivery contract — T10 SAFe cadence and MSP tranches (retrospective, U5a)' (01a20289-2b08-7ea3-96f6-b2ac928a7be4) is live and is the Phase-F obligation this Statement authorises. It binds the project to acceptance/programme/T10.toml, the tranche-4 capacity and WIP limits, the named test evidence, the published PI plan and PI objectives, and the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. Its review 01a2028a-3c4e-7a50-8ee9-d59ad0f11396 records level compliant, as does this Statement's prior review 01a211c9-1a1a-7fac-9b11-7dae24af7b9a; those are the contract reviews, not the new verdict. The Phase-G verdict this pass records is consistent, and the remaining limits are the findings of that review.

## Metadata

Type matrix; phase A; plateau psa; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d36-70c1-a5e8-f50956c5e3f9; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Nine stakeholders on the influence/interest/engagement axes. The sponsoring group decides the tranche exit and the benefit decision. The SRO and BCM are accountable, although benefit ownership remains a free-text role string rather than a job key, which v1-p83-3 records. The Architecture Board approves the seven A–D artefacts, the charter and the delivery contract. The ART and board operator run the PI and accept the materialised cards and the demo; product owners own the backlog and its refinement flags; project managers supply the accepted evidence the demo credit reads; delivery teams receive the materialised cards; and PMO and audit read the tranche review, baselines, benefit status and risk register.

## Links

Reuses the programme roles already recorded in the conveyor buildout programme and the seven A–D artefact set of project T10. The tranche-4 PI plan 01a211c9-1346-7108-9a44-667ebf08b50f names the ART and the ten-project capacity the cadence serves.

The stakeholder view sits under the project's architecture set and the tranche-4 governance record. The engagement values describe the role each stakeholder holds in the cadence and tranche machinery at the 2026-11-24 snapshot; they do not assert that every engagement has occurred.

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase A; plateau psa; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d36-70c1-a5e8-f50956c5e3f9; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Ten driver-goal pairs. D1–D3 cover the WSJF arithmetic and its refusals: no stored score, a WIP bound on materialisation, and a positive job size. D4 is backlog refinement, which flags stale or unscored rows and clears the flag when a row scores again. D5–D6 are the approved-plan gate and the idempotent cadence tick. D7 is the demo evidence gate; D8 is the retro lesson rule; D9 is the tranche review evidence, open on v1-p83-1 and v1-p83-4; and D10 is benefit realization, open in part on v1-p83-2 and v1-p83-3. Each pair names the test functions that record the goal, taken from the project's artefact entries rather than re-executed by this pass.

## Links

Derives from the SPEC_V2 §12 T10 gate and acceptance/programme/T10.toml. Realizes the Phase A driver-goal view over the programme cadence and tranche machinery; reuses the T1 plan-spine vocabulary (wbs_node, project_baseline, programme_tranche) rather than introducing a second planning store.

## Document

The catalog records the intent the slice answers. Two of its ten goals are open at the snapshot: the tranche review accepts placeholders and the benefit transition compares no typed value pair. The catalog states that rather than claiming conformance.

## Metadata

Type diagram; phase A; plateau psa; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d36-70c1-a5e8-f50956c5e3f9; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Ten nodes and flows. The approved PI plan is the gate on materialisation: programme_cadence drives cadence::tick, a wbs_node carries the four typed WSJF inputs, and a card is drafted per deliverable within the WIP slots. An accepted deliverable earns a programme_demo_credit only with a typed evidence array. A retro card must teach every finding as a lesson before it closes. The MSP unit is programme_tranche with programme_tranche_review as its continue, pause or stop gate, and benefit_transition records a measured baseline before a realized status. Two defects are drawn rather than hidden: the tranche-review key check is presence-only (v1-p83-1) and programmes.update is a bypass edge to closed (v1-p83-5).

## Metadata

Type diagram; phase B; plateau hld; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board (conveyor-architecture-board); review date 2026-11-24; project 01a1d039-0d36-70c1-a5e8-f50956c5e3f9; retrospective under delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.

## Entries

Ten capabilities; seven live and three partial. Live: computed WSJF, WIP-bounded materialisation, approved-plan-only materialisation, the idempotent PI tick, backlog refinement, the demo evidence gate and retro lessons. # Project brief — T10 SAFe cadence and MSP tranches (retrospective, 2026-11-24)

## Outcome

T10 is the conveyor's SAFe cadence and MSP tranche slice: PI planning that materialises cards from the backlog by computed WSJF within WIP, a system demo that cannot credit a deliverable without typed evidence, an inspect-and-adapt cycle that cannot close with an untaught finding, an end-of-tranche review that must cite baselines, benefit status and risk evidence, and a benefit transition that cannot report realization without a measured baseline. The register records the project as built and closed at version 15, created 2026-11-12T14:46:02Z and updated 2026-11-24T17:04:34Z, with meta adm_phase G, plateau capability, track v2, tranche 4, viability rework, measured_status built, plan_status draft, expected outputs project-brief and evidence, and both linked issues #82 and #502 closed. This retrospective reconstructs the lifecycle record — charter, seven Phase A–D artefacts, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, WBS deliverable and Phase-G review — around that closure and re-closes the project on 2026-11-24 against acceptance/programme/T10.toml; it does not claim a contemporaneous gate run.

## Boundary

Out of scope: the decision ladder (T2), the plan-spine baseline contract (T1), the coach card (T4) except the retro card, metrics and metering (T11), the one-organisation-loop acceptance (T12), and T19's meeting types, whose binding to the board and cadence §12 records as a follow-up integration unit. T10 must not create a second plan store, a second card store or a stored WSJF score; it reuses T1's wbs_node, project_baseline and shared_config, and S05's card table. Benefit realization happens only through a measured benefit_transition, never through a free-text status.

## Reuse sources

- docs/SPEC_V2.md §8.2 (SAFe as the programme cadence) and §8.3 (MSP as the programme definition and benefits realization); §12 T10 row for the gate.
- T1 plan spine: wbs_node, project_baseline, project_register_item, project_dependency, shared_config and cadence; programme_tranche, benefit_profile and benefit_link per §12 T1.
- T3 PM job: charter, WBS, baseline, staffing, gate routing and closure per §12 T3, and the P0 programme record set.

## Inception units

The inception record is the tranche-4 PI plan and its refinement, not a separate analysis document. The refinement cadence 01a202a2-2705-7392-a2d1-03ca2b3a174e records T10 at 22 open packages (0 P0, 3 P1, 19 P2) and reorders T9 and T10 first by an ART decision over the computed WSJF score. Issues #82 and #502 are closed; no contemporaneous charter, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, Phase A–D artefact body or Phase-G review existed before the retrospective passes.

## Dependencies
